4800.s: to continue to live in common with, i.e. co-survive (literally or figuratively)
t: συν-ζάω (Rec. συζ-), to live with: opposite to συναποθανεῖν, 2Co.7:3; of life in union with Christ, here and hereafter, Rom.6:8, 2Ti.2:11.† (AS)

4801.d: from G4862 and the base of G2201;
4801.s: to yoke together, i.e. (figuratively) conjoin (in marriage)
t: συν-ζεύγνυμι (Rec. συζ-), [in LXX: Eze.1:11, 23 (חָבַר) * ;] to yoke to­gether: metaphorically, of union in wedlock, Mat.19:6, Mrk.10:9.† (AS)

4802.s: to investigate jointly, i.e. discuss, controvert, cavil
t: συν-ζητέω (Rec. συζ-), -ῶ, [in LXX: Neh.2:4 AB1 (בָּקַשׁ pi.) * ;] 1. to search or examine together (Plat.). 2. In NT (and π., see MM, xxiii; also in MGr., see Kennedy, Sources, 155), to discuss, dispute: Mrk.1:27 12:28, Luk.24:15; before quæst. indir., Mrk.9:10; with dative of person(s), Mrk.8:11 Act.6:9; before πρός, with accusative of person(s), Mrk.9:14, 16, Act.9:29; id. before quæst. indir., Luk.22:23.† (AS)
συν-ζήτηαις (Rec. συζ-), -εως, ἡ disputation: Act.28:29 (WH, R, txt., om.).† (AS)

4805.s: co-yoked, i.e. (figuratively) as noun, a colleague; probably rather as a proper name; Syzygus, a Christian
t: σύν-ζυγος (Rec. ουζ-), or as WH, mg., Σύνζυγος, -ον (συνζεύγνυμι), [in Aq., Eze.23:21 * ;] a yoke fellow. Prob., as proper name, Σ. γνήσιε, genuinely Synzygus, S. properly so-called, Php.4:3 (see ICC, Lft., in l; MM, xxiii).† (AS)
συν-ζωο-ποιέω (Rec. συζ-), ῶ-, to make alive or quicken together with; metaphorically, of the spiritual life: τ. Χριστῷ, Eph.2:5; σὺν τ. Χ., Col.2:13.† (AS)

4807.d: of Hebrew origin (H8256) in imitation of G4809;
t: συκάμινος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX for שִׁקְמָה (pl.) ;] the mulberry tree (Lat. morus; cf. μόρον, 1Ma.6:34 *), the sycamine: Luk.17:6. (In LXX, σ. appears to represent the συκόμορος (see: συκομορέα), but St. Luke distinguishes between the two; see ICC, in l; DB, iv, 634.) † (AS)
συκῆ (contr. fr. συκέα), -ῆς, ἡ (σῦκον), [in LXX for תְּאֵן ;] a fig-tree: Mat.21:19-21 24:32, Mrk.11:13, 20-21 13:28, Luk.13:6-7 21:29, Jhn.1:49, 51, Jas.3:12, Rev.6:13.† (AS)

συκο-μορέα (Rec. -μωραία, L, -μωρέα), -ας, ἡ, more commonly (so Aq., Sm., Psa.78:47, Isa.9:10) συκόμορος (σῦκον + μόρον, the black mulberry), a fig-mulberry, a sycamore: Luk.19:4 (cf. συκάμινος).† (AS)
σῦκον, -ου, τό [in LXX for תְּאֵן ] a fig: Mat.7:16, Mrk.11:13, Luk.6:44 Jas.3:12.† (AS)

4811.d: from a compound of G4810 and a derivative of G5316;
4811.s: to be a fig-informer (reporter of the law forbidding the exportation of figs from Greece), "sycophant", i.e. (genitive and by extension) to defraud (exact unlawfully, extort)
4811.k: accuse falsely, take by false accusation.
t: συκοφαντέω, -ῶ (σῦκον, φαίνω), [in LXX: Gen.43:18 (גָּלַל hithpo.), Lev.19:11 (שָׁקַר pi.), Job.35:9, Psa.119:122, Pro.14:31 2:16 28:3, Ecc.4:1 (עָשַׁק) ;] to act the συκοφάντης (on conjectures as to the origin of the term, see LS, see word), to accuse falsely (Aristoph., Xen., al.): Luk.3:14 (R, mg.) Luk.19:8 (RV, exact wrongfully; but cf. Hatch, Essays, 89 ff., see also Field, Notes, 56 f.; MM, xxiv).† (AS)

4812.d: from the base of G4813 and (the reduplicated form of) G71;
4812.s: to lead away as booty, i.e. (figuratively) seduce
t: συλαγωγέω, -ῶ (σύλη, booty + ἄγω), to carry off as spoil, lead captive (θυγατέρα, Heliod., Aeth., 10, 35): metaphorically, Col.2:8.† (AS)

4813.d: from a derivative of σύλλω (to strip;
4813.s: probably akin to G138; compare G4661); to despoil
t: συλάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Ep. Jer.1:18 * ;] with accusative of person(s), to strip, plunder, spoil: 2Co.11:8.† (AS)

4815.s: to clasp, i.e. seize (arrest, capture); specially, to conceive (literally or figuratively); by implication, to aid
t: συλ-λαμβάνω [in LXX for תָּפַשׂ, הָרָה, etc. ;] 1. with accusative, to bring together, collect. 2. to seize, take: with accusative of person(s), as a prisoner, Mat.26:55, Mrk.14:48, Luk.22:54, Jhn.18:12, Act.1:16 12:3; pass., Act.23:27; mid., in sense of act., Act.26:21; σ. ἄγραν ἰχθύων, Luk.5:9. 3. C. dative of person(s), to take part with, assist, succour; mid., in same sense: Luk.5:7, Php.4:3. 4. Of a woman, to conceive: absol., Luk.1:24; before ἐν γαστρί, Luk.1:31; with accusative, Luk.1:36; ib. before ἐν τ. κοιλίᾳ, Luk.2:21; metaphorically, of lust producing sin, Jas.1:15.† (AS)

4816.d: from G4862 and G3004 in its original sense;
t: συλ-λέγω [in LXX chiefly for לָקַט ;] to bring together, collect, gather up: with accusative of thing(s), Mat.13:28-30; pass., Mat.13:40; with accusative, before ἀπό, Mat.7:16; id. before ἐκ, Mat.13:41, Luk.6:44; before εἰς, Mat.13:48.† (AS)

4817.s: to reckon together (with oneself), i.e. deliberate
t: συλ-λογίζομαι [in LXX chiefly for חָשַׁב pi. ;] 1. to compute. 2. to reason: Luk.20:5.† (AS)

4818.s: to afflict jointly, i.e. (passive) sorrow at (on account of) someone
t: συν-λυπέω (Rec. συλλ-), -ῶ, [in LXX: Psa.69:20, Isa.51:19 (נוּד) * ;] to make to grieve with (Arist.). Pass., to be moved to grief by sympathy: before ἐπί, with dative, Mrk.3:5.† (AS)

4819.d: from G4862 and the base of G939;
4819.s: to walk (figuratively, transpire) together, i.e. concur (take place)
t: συμ-βαίνω [in LXX for עָשָׂה, קָרָא, קָרָה, etc. ;] 1. to stand with the feet together. 2. to come together, come to terms. 3. Of events, to come to pass, happen: with dative of person(s), Mrk.10:32, Act.3:10 20:19, 1Co.10:11, 1Pe.4:12, 2Pe.2:22; absol., τὰ σνμβεβηκότα, Luk.24:14 (cf. 1Ma.4:26); with accusative and nf., Act.21:35.† (AS)

4820.s: to combine, i.e. (in speaking) to converse, consult, dispute, (mentally) to consider, (by implication) to aid, (personally) to join, attack
4820.k: confer, encounter, help, make, meet with, ponder.
t: συν-βάλλω (Rec. συμ-), [in LXX: 2Ch.25:19 (גָּרָה hith.), Isa.46:6 (זוּל), Jer.43:3 (סוּת hi.), Wis.5:8, al. ;] to throw together, hence, (a) of speech (before λόγους, Eur., al.), to discuss, confer (sc. λόγους): with dative of person(s), Luk.11:53, WH, mg., Act.17:18; before πρὸς ἀλλήλους, Act.4:15; (b) to reflect, consider, ponder: ἐν τ. καρδίᾳ, Luk.2:19; (with) to meet with, fall in with: Act.20:14; in hostile sense, εἰς πόλεμον, with dative (εἰς μάχην, Polyb.), Luk.14:31; (d) mid., to contribute (Polyb., al.; cf. MM, xxiv): Act.18:27.† (AS)

συμ-βουλεύω [in LXX chiefly for יָעַץ ;] 1. to advise, counsel: with dative of person(s), Jhn.18:14; id. before inf., Rev.3:18. 2. Mid., to take counsel, consult: before ἵνα, Mat.26:4 ("reciprocal middle," see M, Pr., 157); with inf., Act.9:23.† (AS)

4822.s: causative (by reduplication) of the base of G939); to drive together, i.e. unite (in association or affection), (mentally) to infer, show, teach
4822.k: compact, assuredly gather, intrust, knit together, prove.
t: συν-βιβάζω (Rec. συμ-), [in LXX: Exo.4:12, 15, Lev.10:11, Jdg.13:8, Psa.32:8 (יָרָה hi.); Exo.18:16, Deu.4:9, Isa.40:13 (יָדַע hi.), Isa.40:14 (בִּין hi.), Da TH Dan.9:22 (שָׂכַל hi.) * ;] 1. to join or knit together, unite: Eph.4:16, Col.2:2 (but see infr.), Col.2:19. 2. to compare, consider, conclude (Plat.): Act.16:10. 3. to deduce, prove, demonstrate (Arist.): Act.9:22. 4. As in LXX ("translation Greek," = ἐμβιβάζω, metaphorically), to teach, instruct: 1Co.2:16 Act.19:33, R, mg. (also in Vg., Col.2:2, instructi, but see supr.).† (AS)

4823.s: to give (or take) advice jointly, i.e. recommend, deliberate or determine
t: 1. to advise, counsel , Lat. consulere alicui, with dative pers. et infinitive, to advise one to do a thing, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. without the infinitive, ς. τινί τι (Herdotus Historicus); ς. τι to recommend a measure, (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;Pass., τὰ συμβουλευόμενα the advice given , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. absolute to advise, give advice , (Sophocles Tragicus); ὁ συμβουλεύων or -εύσας, an adviser , Lat. auctor sententiae, (Aristotle Philosopher) 4. Mid. to consult with a person, i. e. ask his advice , Lat. consulere aliquem, with dative, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: absolute to consult, deliberate , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

4824.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4825;
4824.s: advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. the provincial assessors or lay-court
t: συμβούλιον, -ου, τό (σύμβουλος), [in LXX: 4Ma.17:17 א * ;] a word of the Græco-Roman period (of. Lat. consilium, and see Deiss., BS, 238) = cl. συμβουλία (Arist., Xen.), 1. counsel: σ. λαμβάνειν, Mat.12:14 22:15 27:7 28:12; διδόναι, Mrk.3:6 (ποιεῖν, Rec.); ποιεῖν, Mrk.15:1 (ἑτοιμάζειν, WH, mg.). 2. By meton., a council (4Mac, l.with א; συνέδριον, AR): Act.25:12 (see MM, xxiv).† (AS)
σύμβουλος, -ου, ὁ (σύν, βουλή), [in LXX for יָעַץ and cogn. forms ;] a counsellor, adviser: Rom.11:34 (LXX).† (AS)

4826.s: Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites
t: Συμεών, ὁ indecl., (Heb. שִׁמְעוֹן), Simeon (so always AV; RV in Luk.2:25, 34 only), Symeon, a Heb. name for which the Gk. Σίμων, which see, was also used; 1. the son of Jacob (Gen.29:33): Rev.7:7. 2. An ancestor of our Lord: Luk.3:30 3. An aged worshipper in the Temple: Luk.2:25, 34. 4. One surnamed Niger: Act.13:1. 5. The apostle Peter: Act.15:14, 2Pe.1:1 (R, txt., WH, txt., Σίμων).† (AS)

Συμεών, ὁ indecl., (Heb. שִׁמְעוֹן), Simeon (so always AV; RV in Luk.2:25, 34 only), Symeon, a Heb. name for which the Gk. Σίμων, which see, was also used; 1. the son of Jacob (Gen.29:33): Rev.7:7. 2. An ancestor of our Lord: Luk.3:30 3. An aged worshipper in the Temple: Luk.2:25, 34. 4. One surnamed Niger: Act.13:1. 5. The apostle Peter: Act.15:14, 2Pe.1:1 (R, txt., WH, txt., Σίμων).† (AS)

Συμεών, ὁ indecl., (Heb. שִׁמְעוֹן), Simeon (so always AV; RV in Luk.2:25, 34 only), Symeon, a Heb. name for which the Gk. Σίμων, which see, was also used; 1. the son of Jacob (Gen.29:33): Rev.7:7. 2. An ancestor of our Lord: Luk.3:30 3. An aged worshipper in the Temple: Luk.2:25, 34. 4. One surnamed Niger: Act.13:1. 5. The apostle Peter: Act.15:14, 2Pe.1:1 (R, txt., WH, txt., Σίμων).† (AS)

4827.d: from a compound of G4862 and G3129;
t: συν-μαθητής (Rec. συμμ-), -οῦ, ὁ a fellow-disciple: Jhn.11:16 (on the use of συν- in such compounds as this, see Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.).† (AS)

4828.s: to testify jointly, i.e. corroborate by (concurrent) evidence
t: συν-μαρτυρέω (Rec. συμμ-), -ῶ, to bear witness with: Rom.2:15; with dative, Rom.8:16; before ὅτι, Rom.9:1.† (AS)

4829.d: middle voice from G4862 and G3307;
4829.s: to share jointly, i.e. participate in
t: συν-μερίζω (Rec. συμμ-), [in LXX: Pro.29:24 א2 (חָלַק) * ;] to distri­bute in shares. Mid., to have a share in: 1Co.9:13 (Diod., al.).† (AS)

συν-μέτοχος (Rec. συμμ-), -ον, partaking together with; as subst., ὁ σ., a joint partaker (with dative of person(s) and genitive of thing(s), FlJ, BJ, i, 24, 6): with genitive of thing(s), Eph.3:6; with genitive of person(s), Eph.5:7 (Arist.).† (AS)

4831.d: from a presumed compound of G4862 and G3401;
t: συν-μιμητής (Rec. συμμ-), -οῦ, ὁ a fellow-imitator: with genitive obj., Php.3:17 (see ICC, in l). Not elsewhere.† (AS)
σύμ-μορφος, -ον (σύν, μορφή), 1. absol., similar (Luc.). 2. con­formed to: with dative, Php.3:21; with genitive, Rom.8:29 (see B1., § 36, 11; 37, 6).† (AS)

4833.s: to render like, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate
t: Pass. to be conformed to , τινι (New Testament) (ML)

4834.s: to feel "sympathy" with, i.e. (by implication) to commiserate
4834.k: have compassion, be touched with a feeling of.
t: συν-παθέω (Rec. συμπ-), -ῶ, [in LXX: 4Ma.5:25 AR 4Ma.13:23 * ;] to have a fellow feeling for or with, sympathize with or in: with dative of thing(s), Heb.4:15; dative of person(s), Heb.10:34 (Arist., Plut., al.).† (AS)

4835.s: having a fellow-feeling ("sympathetic"), i.e. (by implication) mutually commiserative
t: συμπαθής, -ές (σύν, πάσχω) [in LXX: Job.29:25 A (אָבֵל), 4Ma.5:25 א, 4Ma.13:23 4Mac 15:4 * ;] 1. affected by like feelings, sympathetic: 1Pe.3:8. 2. exciting sympathy (Jb, l.with; Dion. H.).† (AS)

4836.s: to be present together, i.e. to convene; by implication, to appear in aid
t: συν-παρα-γίνομαι (Rec. συμπ-), [in LXX: Psa.83:8 (לָוָה ni.) * ;] 1. to come up or be present together: before ἐπί, Luk.23:48. 2. to come up to assist (Thuc., al.; 2Ti.4:16, Rec.).† (AS)
συν-παρα-καλέω (Rec. συμπ-), -ῶ, to call upon or exhort together (Plat.). Pass., to be strengthened or comforted with and among: Rom.1:12.† (AS)

συν-παρα-λαμβάνω (Rec. συμπ-), [in LXX: Gen.19:17 (סָפָה ni.), Job.1:4 (שָׁלַח ni), 3Ma.1:1 * ;] to take along with: as a companion, with accusative, Act.12:25 15:37-38 (on the tenses, see M, Pr., 130), Gal.2:1.† (AS)

4839.s: to remain in company, i.e. still live

4840.s: to be at hand together, i.e. now present
t: συν-πάρειμι (Rec. σνμπ-), [in LXX: Tob.12:12 ΑΒ, Pro.8:27 (?), Wis.9:10 * ;] to be present together or with: with dative of person(s), Act.25:24.† (AS)

4841.d: from G4862 and G3958 (including its alternate);
4841.s: to experience pain jointly or of the same kind (specially, persecution; to "sympathize")
t: συν-πάσχω (Rec. συμπ-), [in Al.: 1Ki.22:8 * ;] 1. to suffer together or with: Rom.8:17, 1Co.12:28. 2. to sympathize with (Plat., Arist.).† (AS)
συν-πέμπω (Rec. συμπ-) to send together with: with accusative and dative, 2Co.8:22; id. before μετά, with genitive, 2Co.8:18.† (AS)

4843.d: from G4862 and a compound of G4012 and G2983;
4843.s: to take by enclosing altogether, i.e. earnestly throw the arms about one
t: συν-περι-λαμβάνω (Rec. συμπ-), 1. to enclose (Eze.5:3 (צוּר) *). 2. to embrace: with accusative of person(s), Act.20:10.† (AS)

4844.s: to partake a beverage in company
t: συμπόσιον, -ου, τό (συμπίνω), [in LXX: Est.7:7 (מִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן) Est.4:17, 1Ma.16:16, 2Ma.2:27, 3Ma.4:16 3Mac 5:36 3Mac 6:33; σ. οἴνου, Sir 34:31 (31:31) Sir.35:5 (32:5), Sir.49:1 * ;] 1. a drinking party 2. By meton., of the party itself, the guests (Plut); pl., σ. σ. (colloq.; see M, Pr., 97), in parties or companies: Mrk.6:39.† (AS)

4845.s: to implenish completely, i.e. (of space) to swamp (a boat), or (of time) to accomplish (passive, be complete)
t: συν-πληρόω (Rec. συμπ-), -ῶ, [in LXX: Jer.25:12 (נָפַל) * ;] 1. to fill up completely (Thuc., of manning ships): of a ship filling with water, and by meton., of those on board, Luk.8:23. 2. to complete, fulfil: of time (Je, l.with, and see MM, xxiv), Luk.9:51, Act.2:1 (on the "durative inf.," see M, Pr., 233).† (AS)

4846.s: to strangle completely, i.e. (literally) to drown, or (figuratively) to crowd
t: συν-πνίγω (Rec. συμπ-), to choke: of thronging by a crowd, Luk.8:42. Fig., of seed, τ. λόγον, Mat.13:22, Mrk.4:7, 19, Luk.8:14.† (AS)

4847.s: a native of the same town, i.e. (figuratively) co-religionist (fellow-Christian)
t: συν-πολίτης (Rec. σνμπ-), -ου, ὁ a fellow-citizen: pl., σ. τ. ἁγίων, opposite to ξένοι κ. πάροικοι, Eph.2:19 (Eur.; C.I., 6446; condemned by Atticists; see Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.).† (AS)

4848.s: to journey together; by implication, to assemble
t: συν-πορεύομαι (Rec. σνμπ-), [in LXX chiefly for הָלַךְ ;] 1. to journey together (Plat., al.): with dative of person(s), Luk.7:11 14:25 24:15. 2. to come together: Mrk.10:1 (Plut., al.).† (AS)

4849.d: neuter of a derivative of the alternate of G4844;
4849.s: a drinking-party ("symposium"), i.e. (by extension) a room of guests
t: 1. a drinking-party, symposium , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc. 2. the room in which such parties were given, drinking-room , (Lucian) (ML)

4851.d: from G4862 and G5342 (including its alternate);
4851.s: to bear together (contribute), i.e. (literally) to collect, or (figuratively) to conduce; especially (neuter participle as a noun) advantage
4851.k: be better for, bring together, be expedient (for), be good, (be) profit(-able for).
t: συμ-φέρω [in LXX: Jer.33:14 (טוֹב), Pro.19:10 (נָאוֶה), Sir.30:19, al. ;] 1. trans. to bring together: with accusative of thing(s), Act.19:19. 2. Intrans., and mostly impers., συμφέρει, it is expedient, profitable or an advantage: 1Co.6:12 10:23, 2Co.8:10; with inf. (M, Pr., 210), Mat.19:10, Jhn.18:14; with dative, before ἵνα (Bl., § 69, 5), Mat.5:29-30 18:6, Jhn.11:50 16:7. Ptcp., ςυμφέρων, profitable: 1Co.12:7; pl., Act.20:20; (οὐ σ. sc. ἐστιν; = οὐ συμφέρει; cf. Thuc., iii, 44, 2), 2Co.12:1; as subst., τὸ σ., profit, Heb.12:10.† (AS)

4852.s: to say jointly, i.e. assent to
t: σύν φημι (Rec. συμ-), to consent, confess: with dative, before ὅτι, Rom.7:16.† (AS)

4853.d: from G4862 and a derivative of G5443;
4853.s: a co-tribesman, i.e. native of the same country
t: συμ-φυλέτης, -ου, ὁ (σύν, φυλή; cf. σύμφυλος, Aq.: Zec.13:7; and see Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.) a fellow-tribesman, fellow-countryman: 1Th.2:14 (see M, Th., in l, and Intr. liii). Not found elsewhere.† (AS)

4854.d: from G4862 and a derivative of G5453;
4854.s: grown along with (connate), i.e. (figuratively) closely united to
t: σύμ-φυτος, -ον (συμφύω, to make to grow together) [in LXX: Zec.11:2 (בָּצַר), Est.7:7 Est.7:8 א2, Amo.9:13, 3Ma.3:22 * ;] 1. congenital, innate (Plat., al.; 3Mac, l.with). 2. grown along with, united with: τ. ὁμοιώματι τ. θανάτου αὐτσῦ (see Field, Notes, 155 f.), Rom.6:5.† (AS)
συν-φύω (Rec. συμ-), [in LXX: Wis.13:13 * ;] to cause to grow together. Pass., to grow together or with (Plat. al.): Luk.8:7.† (AS)

4856.s: to be harmonious, i.e. (figuratively) to accord (be suitable, concur) or stipulate (by compact)
t: συμ-φωνέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Gen.14:3 (H2266) 2Ki.12:8 (9) (H225 ni.), Isa.7:2 (H5117), 4Ma.14:6 * ;] prop., to agree in sound, be in harmony (Plat., Arist.). Metaphorical, (a) to agree with, agree together: Luk.5:36; with dative of thing(s), Act.15:15; before περί, Mat.18:19; pass., with dative of person(s), συνεφωνήθη ὑμῖν, Act.5:9; (b) to agree as to a price (Polyb., Diod.): with dative of person(s), genitive pret., Mat.20:13; before μετά . . . ἐκ, Mat.20:2.† (AS)
συμ-φώνησις, -εως, ἡ (συμφωνέω), concord, agreement: before πρός, with accusative of person(s), 2Co.6:15.† (AS)

4858.s: unison of sound ("symphony"), i.e. a concert of instruments (harmonious note)
t: συμφωνία, -ας, ἡ (σύμφωνος), [in LXX: Dan LXX TH Dan.3:5, 15, TH Dan.3:7, 10 (סוּמְפּוֹנְיָה) 4Ma.14:3 A * ;] 1. symphony, music: Luk.15:25 2. a musical instrument (Polyb., al.; Da, ll. with; v MM, xxiv).† (AS)

4859.s: sounding together (alike), i.e. (figuratively) accordant (neuter as noun, agreement)
t: σύμφωνος, -ον (ούν, φωνή), [in LXX: Ecc.7:14 (עֻמָּה), 4Ma.7:7 4Mac 14:7 * ;] agreeing in sound. Metaphorical, harmonious, agreeing: ἐκ συμφώνου (for exx. from π., see Deiss., BS, 255), by agreement, 1Co.7:5.† (AS)
συμ-ψηφίζω [in LXX: Jer.29:20 (Jer.49:20) A * ;] to reckon together, count up: Act.19:19.† (AS)

4862.s: with or together (but much closer than G3326 or G3844), i.e. by association, companionship, process, resemblance, possession, instrumentality, addition, etc.
t: σύν (old Att. ξύν), prep. with dative, expressing association, fellowship and inclusion. It gradually gave way to μετά, with genitive (cf. LS, see word; Bl., §41, 3), and is therefore comparatively infrequent in NT, being rare in Mat.4, Mrk.6, Jhn.3, and elsewhere (exx. Jas.1:11, 2Pe.1:18) only in Lk (Gosp. and Ac) and Paul. With, together with: of companionship and association, Luk.2:13, Jhn.21:3, Act.10:23, al.; εἶναι σύν τινι, Luk.7:12, Act.4:13, Php.1:23, al.; of partisanship, Act.4:13; οἱ σύν τινι, of attendants, companions or colleagues, Mrk.2:26, Luk.5:9, Act.5:17, al.; of assistance, ἡ χάρις τ. θεοῦ σὺν ἐμοί, 1Co.15:10; of two or more things together, almost = καί, Luk.23:11, Act.3:4 10:2 14:5 23:25, Eph.3:18; σὺν Χριστῷ ζῆν, 2Co.13:4; besides (FlJ, LXX), σὺν πᾶσι τούτοις, Luk.24:21. In composition: with (συνχαίρω), together (συνωδίνω), altogether (συντελέω) (AS)

4863.s: to lead together, i.e. collect or convene; specially, to entertain (hospitably)
4863.k: + accompany, assemble (selves, together), bestow, come together, gather (selves together, up, together), lead into, resort, take in.
t: συν-άγω [in LXX chiefly for אָסַף, also for קָבַץ, etc. (cf. Kennedy, Sources, 128) ;] to gather or bring together: of things, Jhn.6:12-13; before εἰς, Mat.3:12, al.; ἐκεῖ, Luk.12:18; ποῦ, Luk.12:17; συναγαγὼν πάντα (sc. εἰς ἀργύριον; see Field, Notes, 68, MM, xxiv), having sold off all: Luk.15:13; of persons, Jhn.11:52; esp. of assemblies, Mat.2:4, Jhn.11:47, Act.14:27, al. Pass., to be gathered or come together: Mat.22:41, Mrk.2:2, Luk.22:66, al.; before ἐπί Mrk.5:21, Act.4:27; πρός, Mat.13:2, Mrk.4:1, al.; εἰς, Rev.19:17; ἐν, Act.11:26; μετά, Mat.28:12; οὗ, Mat.18:20; ὅπου, Mat.26:57; ἐκεῖ, Jhn.18:2, al. In late writers (see Kennedy, Sources, 128; cf. Deu.22:2, al.), to receive hospitably, entertain: Mat.25:35, 38 25:43 (cf. ἐπι-συνάγω) (AS)

4864.s: an assemblage of persons; specially, a Jewish "synagogue" (the meeting or the place); by analogy, a Christian church
t: συν-αγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for עֵדָה, also for קָהָל, etc. ;] prop., a bringing together; 1. of things, (a) a gathering in of harvest; (b) a collection of money. 2. Of persons, (a) a collecting, assembling (Polyb.); (b) an assembly (MM, xxiv; Deiss., LAE, 101 ff.): Rev.2:9 3:9; esp. of a Jewish religious assembly, a synagogue: Luk.12:11, Act.9:2, al.; of a Christian assembly, Jas.2:2. By meton., of the building in which the assembly is held, a synagogue: Mat.10:17, Mrk.1:21, al. (cf. Cremer, see word ἐκκλησία) SYN.: ἐκκλησία (which see) (AS)

4865.s: to struggle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to be a partner (assistant)
t: συν-αγωνίζομαι to strive together with, to help (prop., of sharing in a contest): with dative of person(s) and of thing(s), Rom.15:30.† (AS)

4866.s: to wrestle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to seek jointly
t: συν-αθλέω, -ῶ = συναγωνίζομαι: with dative commod., Php.1:27; with dative of person(s), before ἐν, Php.4:3.† (AS)

συν-αθροίζω [in LXX chiefly for קָבַץ ;] to gather together, assemble: with accusative of person(s), Act.19:25; pass., Act.12:12.† ἀθροίζω (ἀθρόος, assembled in crowds, MM, VGT, see word; θρόος, a noise, tumult), [in LXX chiefly for קָבַץ ;] to Gather, assemble: Luk.24:33.† (AS)

4868.s: to make up together, i.e. (figuratively) to compute (an account)
t: συν-αίρω [in LXX: Exo.23:5 (עָזַב) * ;] to take up together: σ. λόγον (of which there are several exx. in π.; see Deiss., LAE, 118 f.; MM, i, xxiv; M, Pr., 160), to settle accounts, Mat.18:23-24; before μετά, C. genitive of person(s), Mat.25:19.† (AS)
συν-αιχμάλωτος, -ου, ὁ a fellow prisoner (prop., of a captive in war, see Lft., Col., 234): Rom.16:7, Col.4:10, Phm 23.† (AS)
συν-ακολουθέω, -ῶ [in LXX: 2Ma.2:4 2Mac 2:6 * ;] to follow along with, accompany: with dative of person(s), Mrk.14:51, Luk.23:49; before μετά, with genitive of person(s), Mrk.5:37.† (AS)
συν-αλίζω [in Al.: Psa.141:4 * ;] to assemble with: Act.1:4 (EV, mg., eating with, but on this rendering and on the force of the Pres. ptcp. here, see Field, Notes, 110).† (AS)
συν-ανα-βαίνω [in LXX for עָלָה ;] to go up with: with dative of person(s), before εἰς, with accusative loc., Mrk.15:41, Act.13:31.† (AS)

4873.s: to recline in company with (at a meal)
4873.k: sit (down, at the table, together) with (at meat).
t: συν-ανά-κειμαι [in LXX: 3Ma.5:39 * ;] to recline with or together at table: Mat.14:9, Mrk.6:22, Luk.7:49 14:15; with dative of person(s), Mat.9:10, Mrk.2:15, Luk.14:10.† (AS)

4874.d: from G4862 and a compound of G303 and G3396;
4874.s: to mix up together, i.e. (figurative) associate with
t: συν-ανα-μίγνυμι (accusative to Bl., 8, -μείγνυμι), [in LXX: Hos.7:8 A ( hithpo.), Eze.20:18 A * ;] to mix up together; pass., reflex, and metaphorically, to associate with (Plut., Ath., al.): 1Co.5:9 5:11, 2Th.3:14 (see M, Th., 117).† (AS)

4875.s: to recruit oneself in company with
t: συν-ανα-παύομαι [in LXX: Isa.11:6 (רָבַץ) * ;] with dative of person(s), to lie down to rest with, sleep with. Metaphorical, to be refreshed in spirit with: Rom.15:32 (L, om.).† (AS)

4876.d: from G4862 and a derivative of G473;
4876.s: to meet with; figuratively, to occur
t: συν-αντάω, -ῶ [in LXX for פָּגַע, פָּגַשׁ, קָרָא, קָרָה, etc. ;] to meet with: with dative of person(s), Luk.9:18, 37 22:10, Act.10:25, Heb.7:1, 10. Metaphorical, of events, to happen, befall (Ding. L., Plut., al.): Act.20:22.† (AS)
συν-άντησις, -εως, ἡ Rec. for ὑπάντησις (which see), Mat.8:34.† (AS)

4878.s: to take hold of opposite together, i.e. co-operate (assist)
t: συν-αντι-λαμβάνομαι [in LXX: Gen.30:8 R (†), Exo.18:22, Num.11:17 (נָשָׂא), Psa.89:21 (כּוּן ni.) * ;] to take hold with at the side for assistance; hence, to take a share in, help in bearing, and generally, help (with various constructions, see LXX, ll. with, Deiss., LAE, 83 f.): with dative, Luk.10:40, Rom.8:26.† (AS)

4879.s: to take off together, i.e. transport with (seduce, passively, yield)
t: συν-απ-άγω [in LXX: Exo.14:6 (לָקַח) * ;] to lead away with or together (Ex, l.with). Pass., metaphorically (as συμπεριφέρομαι, see LS, see word), to be carried away with: with dative, Gal.2:13, 2Pe.3:17; of accommodating one­self to (EV, condescend to) things or persons (on the meaning, see ICC, in I.; Field, Notes, 163), Rom.12:16.† (AS)

4880.s: to decease (literally) in company with, or (figuratively), similarly to
t: συν-απο-θνήσκω [in LXX: Sir.19:10 * ;] to die with or together: Mrk.14:31, 2Co.7:3 (see Meyer, in l), 2Ti.2:11.† (AS)

4881.s: to destroy (middle voice or passively, be slain) in company with
t: συν-απ-όλλυμι [in LXX chiefly for סָפָה ;] to destroy with or together. Pass., to perish together (with): with dative of person(s), Heb.11:31.† (AS)

4882.s: to despatch (on an errand) in company with
t: συν-απο-στέλλω [in LXX: Exo.33:2, 12 (שָׁלַח), I Est.5:2 * ;] to send along with: with accusative, 2Co.12:18 (cf. MM, xxiv).† (AS)

4883.d: from G4862 and a derivative of a compound of G719 and G3004 (in its original sense of laying);
4883.s: to render close-jointed together, i.e. organize compactly
t: συν-αρμολογέω, -ῶ (ἁρμός, λέγω), = cl. συναρμόζω, to fit or frame together: of the parts of a building, Eph.2:21; of the members of the body, Eph.4:16 (Eccl.).† (AS)

συν-αρπάζω [in LXX: Pro.6:25 (לָקַח), 2Ma.3:27 2Mac 4:41, 4Ma.5:4 * ;] "perfective " of ἁοπάζω (see M, Pr., 113), (a) to seize and carry away (so most commonly) : Act.27:15; (b) to seize and hold: Luk.8:29, Act.6:12 19:29.† (AS)
συν-αυξάνω [in LXX: 2Ma.4:4, 4Ma.13:27 * ;] to cause to increase or grow together. Pass., to grow together: Mat.13:30 (Xen., al.).† (AS)

4886.s: a joint tie, i.e. ligament, (figuratively) uniting principle, control
t: σύν-δεσμος, -ου, ὁ (συνδέω), [in LXX for קֶשֶׁר, קְטַר, etc. ;] that which binds together, a bond: of the ligaments of the body, Col.2:19. Metaphorical, σ. ἀδικίας, Act.8:23; τ. τελειότητος, Col.3:14; τ. εἰρήνης, Eph.4:3 (see Lft., Col., ll. with).† (AS)

4887.s: to bind with, i.e. (passively) be a fellow-prisoner (figuratively)
t: συν-δέω [in LXX for שָׁבַץ, etc. ;] (a) to bind together; (b) to bind together with: pass., Heb.13:3.† (AS)

4888.s: to exalt to dignity in company (i.e. similarly) with
t: συν-δοξάζω 1. to join in approving (Arist.). 2. In NT only, to glorify together: pass., Rom.8:17.† (AS)

4889.s: a co-slave, i.e. servitor or ministrant of the same master (human or divine)
t: σύν-δουλος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Est.4:7, 9 4:17, 23 5:3, 6 6:6, 13 (כְּנָת) * ;] a fellow-servant: Mat.18:28-33 24:49; of servants of the same divine Lord, Col.1:7 4:7, Rev.6:11; so of angels, Rev.19:10 22:9.† (AS)
συνδρομή, -ῆς, ἡ (συντρέχω), [in LXX: Jdth.10:18, 3Ma.3:8 * ;] concourse, esp. of a riotous gathering: Act.21:30 (Arist., Polyb., al.).† (AS)

4891.s: to rouse (from death) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to revivify (spirtually) in resemblance to
t: συν-εγείρω [in LXX: Exo.23:5 B2 (עָזַב), Isa.14:9 (עוּר pil.), 4Ma.2:14 * ;] to raise together: metaphorically, of the Christian's mystical resur­rection with Christ, Eph.2:6; pass., Col.2:12 3:1.† (AS)

4892.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of G4862 and the base of G1476;
4892.s: a joint session, i.e. (specially), the Jewish Sanhedrin; by analogy, a subordinate tribunal
t: συνέδριον, -ου, τό (σύν + ἕδρα, a seat) [in LXX: Pro.11:13 15:22, Jer.15:17 (סוֹד), Psa.26:4 (מַת), Pro.22:10 (דִּין) Pro.26:26 (קָהָל); Pro.24:7 27:22 31:23, 2Ma.14:5, 4Ma.17:17 * ;] 1. a council (Plat., Xen., al.; LXX; in π., σ. τ. πρεσβυτέρων, Deiss., BS, 156): of a local Jewish tribunal, Mat.10:17, Mrk.13:9. 2. The supreme ecclesiastical court of the Jews, the Sanhedrin (i.e. Talmudic סַנְהֵדְרִין = συνέδριον): Mat.5:22 26:59, Mrk.14:55 15:1, Luk.22:66, Act.5:21, 27 5:34, 41 6:12, 15 22:30 23:1, 6 23:15, 20 23:28 (WH, R, mg., om.) Act.24:20 of a meeting of the Sanhedrin, Jhn.11:47; of the place of meeting, Act.4:15.† (AS)

4893.d: from a prolonged form of G4894;
t: συν-είδησις, -εως, ἡ (συνεῖδον), [in LXX: Ecc.10:20 (מַדָּע), Wis.17:11, Sir.42:18 א * ;] 1. consciousness: with genitive obj., Heb.10:2, 1Pe.2:19. 2. In ethical sense, innate discernment, self-judging consciousness, conscience (Stoics and late writers): Rom.2:15 9:1, 1Co.10:29, 2Co.1:12 4:2 5:11, 1Ti.4:2, Heb.9:14; σ. ἀγαθή, Act.23:1, 1Ti.1:5 1:19, 1Pe.3:16 3:21; ἀσθενής, 1Co.8:7 8:10; ἀσθενοῦσα, 1Co.8:12; ἀπρόσκοπος, Act.24:16; καθαρά, 1Ti.3:9, 2Ti.1:3; καλή, Heb.13:18; πονηρά, Heb.10:22; ὁ νοῦς καὶ ἡ σ., Tit.1:15; διὰ τὴν σ., Rom.13:5, 1Co.10:25 10:27-28; κατὰ σ., Heb.9:9; ὑπὸ (τῆς) σ., Jhn.8:1-59 [9] (Rec.), 1Co.10:29 (cf. Cremer, 233 ff.; ICC on Rom.2:15; DB, i, 468 ff.).† (AS)

4894.s: to see completely; used (like its primary) only in two past tenses, respectively meaning to understand or become aware, and to be conscious or (clandestinely) informed of
4894.k: consider, know, be privy, be ware of.
t: συν-εῖδον irreg. aorist of συνοράω (see: εἶδον), [in LXX: 1Ma.4:21 א, 2Ma.2:24 2Mac 4:4 2Mac 4:41 R 2Ma.5:17 2Mac 7:4 2Mac 7:20 2Mac 8:8, 3Ma.2:8 A * ;] 1. to see together or at the same time (Arist., Xen.). 2. to see in one view, hence, of mental vision, to comprehend, understand (LXX, Polyb., Plut., al.) : Act.12:12 14:6 (on the related σύνοιδα, see see word).† (AS)

ύν-οιδα , pf. with Pres. meaning (see: οἶδα), [in LXX: Lev.5:1 (יָדַע), Job.27:6; ptcp., 1Ma.4:21 A, 2Ma.4:41 A, 3Ma.2:8 R * ;] 1. to share the knowledge of, be privy to (Hdt., Thuc., al.): ptcp., Act.5:2. 2. C. prop. reflex., to be conscious of (Eur., Plat., al.), esp. of guilty consciousness: οὐδὲν γὰρ ἐμαυτῷ σ., for I know nothing against myself, 1Co.4:4.† (AS)

4895.d: from G4862 and G1510 (including its various inflections);
4895.s: to be in company with, i.e. present at the time
t: σύν-ειμι (εἰμί to be), [in LXX: Jer.3:20 (רֵעַ), al. ;] to be with: Luk.9:18 (WH, mg., συνήντησαν), Act.22:11.† (AS)

4897.k: go in with, go with into.
t: συν-εισ-έρχομαι [in LXX: Job.22:4 (עִם בּוֹא), etc. ;] to enter together: with dative of person(s), before εἰς, with accusative loc., Jhn.6:22 18:15.† (AS)

4898.d: from G4862 and the base of G1553;
4898.s: a co-absentee from home, i.e. fellow-traveller

4899.d: from a compound of G4862 and G1586;
4899.s: chosen in company with, i.e. co-elect (fellow Christian)
t: συν-εκ-λεκτός, -ή, -όν chosen together with, co-elect: ἡ ἐν Βαβυλῶνι συνεκλεκτή (on the meaning, see ICC, in l), 1Pe.5:13.† (AS)
